description: A project's ratio is its total boxx divided by its total boxz.

b.request: For each project with a matching spatial record, divide the sum of its nonmissing `boxx` values by the sum of its nonmissing `boxz` values; compare that ratio with the simple average of project ratios in the same funding source, and return the 10 projects with the largest positive margins, showing project ID, funding source, ratio, and margin, sorted by margin descending with missing margins last and no rounding
b.sql: WITH project_ratios AS (SELECT p.arcregistry AS project_id, p.fundflux AS funding_source, SUM(s.boxx) / NULLIF(SUM(s.boxz), 0) AS ratio FROM projects p JOIN scanspatial s ON s.arcref = p.arcregistry GROUP BY p.arcregistry, p.fundflux), compared AS (SELECT project_id, funding_source, ratio, ratio - AVG(ratio) OVER (PARTITION BY funding_source) AS margin FROM project_ratios) SELECT project_id, funding_source, ratio, margin FROM compared WHERE margin > 0 ORDER BY margin DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;

a.request: Match each spatial record (`scanspatial`) to the project whose `arcregistry` equals its `arcref`, and drop records with no matching project. For each project ID and its funding source (`projects.fundflux`), work out the project's X-to-Z ratio like this: add up all of its `boxx` values and, separately, all of its `boxz` values (ignoring missing ones), then divide the `boxx` total by the `boxz` total. Within each funding source, take the simple average of its projects' ratios. Then return the 10 projects whose ratio is above their funding source's average by the most. Sort them by that excess from largest to smallest, with missing values last. Show the project ID, funding source, ratio and excess, with no rounding.
a.sql: WITH project_ratios AS (SELECT p.arcregistry AS project_id, p.fundflux AS funding_source, SUM(s.boxx) / NULLIF(SUM(s.boxz), 0) AS ratio FROM scanspatial AS s INNER JOIN projects AS p ON p.arcregistry = s.arcref GROUP BY p.arcregistry, p.fundflux), ranked AS (SELECT project_id, funding_source, ratio, ratio - AVG(ratio) OVER (PARTITION BY funding_source) AS excess FROM project_ratios) SELECT project_id, funding_source, ratio, excess FROM ranked WHERE excess > 0 ORDER BY excess DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;

c.request: Match each spatial record (`scanspatial`) to the project whose `arcregistry` equals its `arcref`, and drop records with no matching project. What is each project's bounding-box X-to-Z ratio (`boxx` to `boxz`), ignoring missing values? Which 10 projects beat the simple average ratio of the projects in their own funding source (`projects.fundflux`) by the widest margin? Show the project ID, funding source, ratio and margin, sorted by margin from largest to smallest (missing last), with no rounding. A project's ratio is its total boxx divided by its total boxz.
c.sql: WITH project_ratios AS (SELECT p.arcregistry AS project_id, p.fundflux AS funding_source, SUM(s.boxx) / NULLIF(SUM(s.boxz), 0) AS ratio FROM scanspatial AS s JOIN projects AS p ON p.arcregistry = s.arcref GROUP BY p.arcregistry, p.fundflux), ranked AS (SELECT project_id, funding_source, ratio, ratio - AVG(ratio) OVER (PARTITION BY funding_source) AS margin FROM project_ratios) SELECT project_id, funding_source, ratio, margin FROM ranked ORDER BY margin DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;

d.request: Match each `scanspatial` record to the project where `projects.arcregistry = scanspatial.arcref`, and exclude records with no matching project. For each project, calculate its bounding-box X-to-Z ratio as the sum of nonmissing `boxx` values divided by the sum of nonmissing `boxz` values. Compare that ratio with the simple average of project ratios within the same `projects.fundflux` funding source. Which 10 projects exceed their funding source’s average by the largest margin? Show the project ID, funding source, ratio, and margin, sorted by margin descending with missing values last, without rounding.
d.sql: WITH project_ratios AS (SELECT p.arcregistry AS project_id, p.fundflux AS funding_source, SUM(s.boxx) / NULLIF(SUM(s.boxz), 0) AS ratio FROM scanspatial AS s JOIN projects AS p ON p.arcregistry = s.arcref GROUP BY p.arcregistry, p.fundflux), compared AS (SELECT project_id, funding_source, ratio, ratio - AVG(ratio) OVER (PARTITION BY funding_source) AS margin FROM project_ratios) SELECT project_id, funding_source, ratio, margin FROM compared WHERE margin > 0 ORDER BY margin DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;
